utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber would like to inform the parties that pursuant to Rule 15 bis (A), today's hearing will take place in the absence of Judge Stole. Judge Stole is ill and Judge Hoepfel and myself concluded that it's in the interests of justice to continue the trial without Judge Stole. As far as we can see, the illness will not take very long. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've asked that we have a moment before the witness is brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to discuss again the question of timing, and I need to ask Your Honour for an extra 30 minutes on the allocation that you had agreed I could have today. In other words, Your Honour had indicated an hour today and I'm going to have to ask Your Honour for an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First session -- I do understand that some new elements came up also in view of the notes which, of course, could not be foreseen at an earlier stage -- at least these are part of the notes which were not copied.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And at the same time I think we had a rather successful meeting this morning on the 92 ter statement of the next witness which will certainly reduce the time in chief we would need for him, and although it was assessed that it would be only 15 minutes I was very much afraid that it would take more.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore I was a bit -- I kept a bit on the safe side in time scheduling. If we get started we lose as little time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I indicate one matter to Your Honour, a detail, before the witness comes in. On the photocopied sheet of notes that you have in front of you, Your Honours may see towards the spine there is a vertical line written on the right-hand side of the spine which ends in a circle around the name Ganimete Gashi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I should indicate those markings were put on the photocopy, the only photocopy, that was provided before these subsequent copies were made. In other words, that line and that circle do not appear on the original in the witness's notebook and I'm just making that clear so that obviously better copies will need to be made in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then curtains down for the witness to be brought in and then we'll continue in open session, although with face and with voice distortion and with pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, just to indicate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For convenience I have had printed out four pages of transcript -- three pages of transcript from yesterday which deal with questions I put to the witness concerning Kemal and Mejdin Gashi and answers the witness gave yesterday which will be helpful --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine as such, but of course the Judges can consulted, as you may have noticed, whatever parted of the transcript or the whole of the trial --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of course. I thought it might be helpful for Your Honours to cast an eye over it as the witness was answering the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I take the opportunity to inform the public that, as we did before, that the Chamber meets with the parties to see to what extent it can assist in resolving discussions about what is appropriately and what is not appropriately introduced in a 92 ter statement. The Chamber encourages the parties to develop such skills that they can do it without the assistance of the Chamber, but up to the moment we are that far the Chamber is available either from 10.00 p.m. Or on from 7.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness 17. I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you gave at the beginning of your testimony. And I'd also like to know whether the original of your notes have been returned to you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Yes, I received them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Mr. Emmerson will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I wonder if the witness could be handed the single sheet of note paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you can just -- for the moment, Witness 17, if you could place that face-down. Yesterday I asked you some questions about a soldier under your command, Mejdin Gashi, and this is transcript 7702 to 7704,, and I asked you about an incident which he has testified about where his father was detained as a suspected collaborator and taken by one of your FARK officers called Musa Dragaj to Mete Krasniqi's office. And you said to us yesterday that although Musa Dragaj was in the brigade you were not aware of the case and you said you knew of no legitimate reason why any of your subordinates could contact or cooperate with Mete Krasniqi over such a case and you were aware of no such cooperation. That was your testimony yesterday morning, Witness 17. Could we now please look -- would you turn over the piece of paper that is in front of you which is an extract from your notebook which you handed to the registrar yesterday, and if you'd like, please, in the original to find on the left-hand side a line that is crossed out. Do you see that? On the front page there, Witness 17, left-hand side towards the bottom there is a line crossed out. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please read slowly for us the words that follow from that so that we have them on the transcript. Read them slowly in Albanian. That is to say the words beneath the crossing out and the whole of the right-hand side of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the place where "Shpetim Berisha" has been crossed out, that's what you want me to read?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, from that place, please, beneath that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Ljumir from Peje has sent Kemal Gashi to the place in Qallapek to see how many soldiers Mete has, the armament, and where they have been stationed. Go towards Loxha. It has been said -- it is supposed that his son" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear what the witness read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I invite you because the interpreters need some time to translate -- to start reading again but very slowly and speaking well into the microphone so that the interpreters can hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May the interpreters note that the interpreters have not found the place where the witness is reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Has the sheet been provided --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, the interpreters have the sheet in the booth. If you look at the Albanian front page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- Left-hand side three-quarters of the way down there is a line crossed out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- And the text begins beneath that line.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please start again reading very slowly so the interpreter can follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There is also a draft translation attached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You know interpreters usually do not work on the basis of draft translations but take their responsibility for correct interpretation. Yes, could you please restart.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. "The security of Peje has sent Kemajl Gashi Mustafa to Peje with a decision in Qallapek to see how many soldiers Mete has, their armament, and how they have been stationed and to observe in the direction of Loxha. It is supposed that his son is in the same direction, Baran" -- no, "he lives in Visegradska, no number, payment 300 Deutschemarks. "Kemajl Gashi - Peje, spy, 20th of the 7th, 1998, works for 300 Deutschemarks. He has been sent to the unit by Dragan Callouci, Bek Mucaj has brought him. He's a businessman, up to Leshan. From Leshan Bek Nici has brought him over here. "Haxhi Kastrati, Raushiq, an academician in the art academy volunteered on the 23rd of July to help the brigade. "Mejdin Gashi, Street Visegrad, in Peje, 19th of the 7th, 1998. "Gani Gashi. "Ganimete Gashi - Mejdin's daughter is suspected to be a collaborator of the police of Serbia. "Soldier in our barracks (he does not know his father and his opinions). "Saban Raucoj, Studenice by Peje he lives" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We can stop the extract there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. During that translation just before the words "soldier in our barracks, "I did hear the witness say "Mejdin Gashi" and it did come over in translation and it doesn't appear at page 7, line 9, and that should read "Mejdin Gashi."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I noticed the same line at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Also on line 6 Afghani Gashi there's the word Buqan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Buqan. I don't know whether the witness read that or not, but the parties have the opportunity to see what the witness -- what the paper was from which the witness read and this is now on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can't see --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- It's sufficient for present purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Whether the witness read -- we can continue on the basis of the corrections.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note the witness mentioned Mejdin Gashi; it was an error on the part of the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for informing us.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Why did you tell us yesterday that you didn't know about this case, Witness 17?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was I supposed to say about this case? I cannot have all the names of all the persons of my brigade in my head. That's why I kept notes. It's impossible to have all the things that are in the documentation in my head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 17, if you have reasons to believe that your memory doesn't serve you in details, you should tell us. If you don't know about it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I wanted to say, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now. You didn't do that yesterday, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I said that I don't know the name of the soldier that was asked of me and it is very true that I cannot remember all the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's all very well, Witness 17, but I specifically put to you that a soldier in your brigade was called by Musa Dragaj to Mete Krasniqi's office because his father was suspected of being a collaborator. And you have in your notebook a note of that very same soldier whose father is suspected of being a collaborator. Let's just be clear about this. Leaving the name aside- and I asked you those questions yesterday, Witness 17 - had you forgotten about this incident altogether?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will say it again that I'm not aware. I do not recall at all such an incident. I was not informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because would you agree that what you have recorded is that Kemal Gashi was suspected of spying on Mete?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the note I see here, this shows that he has been sent for this. But I did not have any other relevant or further facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that would be Mete Krasniqi, would it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you knew that an allegation was being made that the father of a soldier in your brigade was spying on Mete Krasniqi. Now, you told us yesterday that there was no legitimate way in which an officer under your command could contact or cooperate with Mete Krasniqi. Can you explain that for us, please, Witness 17, because here we have you in your own notebook recording that the father of one of your soldiers is spying on Mete Krasniqi and yesterday you told us that he was no part of your structure and that your officers could not legitimately cooperate with him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's what I said yesterday, but in the operational zone of the brigade where I needed to be informed about all the things that were going on, and that's why I have this information in my notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so who do you think would have given you that information that you wrote in your notebook, Witness 17, would it have been one of your officers or Mete Krasniqi himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not noted it down; that is to say, I have not noted down who gave me this information, and I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's perfectly plain -- it is perfectly plain, I suggest, from this passage that at the time you wrote this note you and your officers were cooperating directly with Mete Krasniqi in the investigation of a suspected collaborator who was the father of one of the soldiers in your barracks. And I suggest that the evidence that you gave to us evidence was a series of deliberate lies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to the form of that question. Nothing about this note suggests that Mete Krasniqi is within the brigade structure of this witness. To suggest that he is lying, I believe, is inappropriate based on that foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is sustained. Mr. Emmerson, the mere fact that you send someone to investigate a person who is spying does not necessarily include -- and therefore your language was too strong as far as direct cooperation between officers and this person is concerned. Please proceed. This is not to say that you could not pursue the matter perhaps in another way, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've heard evidence, Witness 17, as you know because I told you about it yesterday, that this young man, Mejdin Gashi, was taken to Mete Krasniqi's office and that it was Mete Krasniqi who was conducting the investigation into the suspected collaboration. If that's right, how did the information end up in your notebook if there was no cooperation between you, your officers, and Mete Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to object again. I'm very sorry to interrupt my colleague, but the form of this question makes it almost impossible for this witness to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see what the answer of the witness all right, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: All right, the ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say that our legitimate structure I never had any contact with Mete Krasniqi about these things first; and second, I said this and I stand by it. Everything that happened in Lugu i Baranit I wanted to know about them, good things, bad things, I wanted to know about them and I noted them down; and third, Mejdin Gashi, he's a soldier in our barracks and he says that he does not know his father and his opinions. I have said this here and it is clear that Mejdin Gashi had nothing to do with Mete Krasniqi or anybody else, according to the notes in my notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And that information about Mejdin Gashi's position came, I suggest, as a result of him being interviewed by Mete Krasniqi, as he has told us, being asked questions by Mete Krasniqi about whether or not he shared his father's position. And so somehow that information that was provided by Mejdin Gashi to Mete Krasniqi has found its way into your notebook.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, all but the last question about how this information got into his notebook calls for speculation on behalf of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. As a matter of fact, how this information comes into his notebook if the witness has written down these notes himself, then he is the one to answer question how that information reached him, which he then did write down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I completely agree with the Trial Chamber. That's what I said, the last sentence about how the notes got there is a worthy area of inquiry, but the speculation about what Mejdin Gashi was thinking is speculation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you write down something, and until now I understood these notes, apart from the second portion of the notes which are the different handwriting and what the witness said that is not what I did write down, where he earlier said what he did write down in his notes, whether he did it the same day or he did it the other way. So the witness is perfectly in a position to tell us where the information came from, he did write down --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think Mr. Kearney may be labouring under a misapprehension as well because what I was putting to the witness was the testimony of Mejdin Gashi that he was interviewed by Mete Krasniqi, not speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. So the question to you now is: Where did you get the information you did write down in your notebook on this matter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During my stay in Lugu i Baranit, I collected information from different persons, first of all, from the commanding structure of the brigade and its elements that I mentioned yesterday. Then I received information from the local village commanders in the Lugu i Baranit and also information from ordinary people. So for the moment, I'm not in the position and I do not recollect who gave me this information that I noted in my notebook.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, Mr. Emmerson has put it to you that what you did write down includes the -- what the son knows about his father and his opinions. And we received evidence that that son was interviewed about this matter, interviewed by Mete Krasniqi. So therefore, the Chamber has to consider that that might be the place and the time and the person to whom he gave this information. Now, since you said there was no legitimate contact between you and Mete Krasniqi, the question arises: How then such information which is likely to have been obtained in this interview reached you. It could not be through village commanders, at least that would need quite a lot of explanation. Therefore, that is what is puzzling Mr. Emmerson and might puzzle the Chamber as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not denying whether this soldier was interviewed by Mete; however, I will repeat it again, that he was not part of the brigade structure since the work of the military police in the Lugu i Baranit went in two directions, and I have notes and documents by Ramush from a meeting on the 26th of the seventh month in Irzniq. He underlined at that meeting that the work of the military police in Lugu i Baranit went in two different directions, one was the military police of the brigade and the second direction was those people who performed those duties before the arrival of the brigade. And he said this clearly. So these two different directions were supposed to melt into one, to become one, or the brigade to have this military police unit within its structure for its own work. This is what I was trying to say yesterday, that the structures, the existing structures before our arrival in Baran and before the formation of the military police within the framework of the brigade were not part of the structure of the command of the brigade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now you are explaining to us again and again and again about the structure. What we're interested to hear about is not about what the formal structure was but what actually happened. Let me put then a few quite simple questions to you. Were you aware that Mete Krasniqi was still functioning de facto, that means in practice, as someone who performed police duties? Whether or not he was part of the structure, whether he was authorised to do that, different question. Was he performing duties which are usually performed by a police officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was part of the structure of the military police before our arrival in the area of Lugu i Baranit and he continued to perform those duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When he continued to perform those duties, were you, whether authorised or not, were you receiving any information resulting from these activities, whether this was in a hierarchy or whether it was within a formal structure, yes or no. I'm not interested in that. I'm just interested in whether you received, whether you obtained, in whatever way, formal, informal, information about the result of this performance of police-like duties.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the beginning, no, but later on, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Talking about mid-July, do you consider it possible that some of what you did write down was information you obtained as a result of Mete Krasniqi's performance of duties? Whether informal or not, I'm not talking about that. Is it possible that this is information that leaked from him -- his activities into your notebook?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a possibility, but I wouldn't be able to say right now who gave me this information because personally I didn't have contacts with Mete Krasniqi regarding these issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Dragan Callouci, was that someone under your command?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did Your Honour mean Musa Dragaj?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I'm talking about Dragan Kaluci. Was that someone under your command? Bek Mucaj was he under your command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. These persons that you mentioned were not there and I don't even know them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, you did write down their names. If you say you don't know them, these are the names we find in your notes, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If they appear on my notes, that does not mean that they were in the brigade and that I knew them. I simply made note of this just to inform myself about the structure of the brigade. I think I am clear and I am sincerely telling you that I didn't know them then. I don't know them now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, you have written down these names in relation to this matter. Now you tell us that you don't know the people, they were not in your brigade. How did you get their names because you did write them down, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is true that I wrote down these names with my own hand, but as I said I received information from different channels. So I'm not able to tell you precisely from where I got this particular information for these notes, from which channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, your notes describe that people were -- and it is under the heading of Kemal Gashi, how they were taken and where they were brought. And then it says "from Leshan Bek Nici takes over and brings them here." And usually if people write down "here" that refers to the place where they are at that moment. Now, we heard evidence about that person being brought to Mete Krasniqi, and we are wondering where you write down that being brought "here," if that would be in Mete Krasniqi's office, which you would not have excluded to be in the area where you were working, how we have to reconcile that with a lack of whatever cooperation between Mete Krasniqi and you and your subordinates and officers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no cooperation between myself and Mete regarding these issues; however, as far as Kemal Gashi's concerned, accordingly to the notes, I think that the person in question is escorting these people from the zone outside and from the zone outside. It is said here that he is working for 300 Deutschemarks, kind of trafficking. This is the meaning that I think these notes have, although I would not be able to tell you precisely whether "here" means Mete Krasniqi's office or Baran. It means the zone because I made all my notes within the frameworks of my zone. I wanted to know what was going on in the zone in general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then finally the name Bek Nici, is that a name familiar to you? Do you know who he is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says "Bek Mucaj." I cannot find "Nici" -- oh, yes, I found it, it's to the bottom. I don't know this person at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just one last question on this document. It says that it is suspected that his son is also of the same direction, and a little later it says Ganimete Gashi is suspected of being a collaborator of the Serbian police. Suspected by whom, Witness 17? Whose suspicion does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the notes, I think I'm very clear that the person who gave me this information came to me and told me these words: It is suspected that this and that, and I recorded this information in my notebook. It's just a note of the information that I received and that further measures would be undertaken to verify this information. This is what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so if you weren't having direct contact with Mete Krasniqi, it follows, doesn't it, that one of your officers was telling you that these people were suspected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This possibility also exists; I'm not denying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because you told us yesterday you could think of no legitimate way with your authorisation that officers under your command could cooperate with Mete Krasniqi. Is that still your answer, in the light of what you've just told us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm going to object to the word "cooperate" as vague. Does that mean communicate or work within a brigade structure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As large as possible --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm using the witness's own words. "I'm not aware of any cooperation, legitimate cooperation, with my authorisation or at my request and I don't know of any legitimate way that my subordinates contacted him or coordinated with him." Those are the witness's words from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we should phrase the question to him in those words "contact" or "cooperate."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think as a matter of fact -- well, so many words have been spoken now since the question. Could you please put the question to the witness again and do it in such a way that we could expect to have no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Given that you accept that one of your officers communicated to you the suspicion against these people, do you still say that you can think of no legitimate circumstances in which your officers could cooperate through the exchange of information about collaborators with Mete Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I will repeat what I said earlier. It may be true that I received this information from my officers. It may be true. The possibility still exists for this information to reach me through other channels, but legitimately I would like to assure you again that there were no direct contacts between myself or my officers and Mete Krasniqi. However, private contacts, daily contacts, or people meeting in the street and exchanging words with each other, this is impossible to prevent and I cannot say with certainty whether there were such contacts or not, but not in -- I don't have knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally this: Do you recall now then, having been told that there were -- that there was a suspected collaborator within your own ranks, do you recall who you gave the responsibility to investigate that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. You said within the ranks --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put it to you again. The information in your notebook puts you on notice that the father of one of your own soldiers is suspected to be a spy, his daughter suspected to be a Serb police collaborator, and that there were suspicions that the son - one of your soldiers under your command - was in the same direction. My question was: Learning that information, what steps, if any, did you take to investigate it and to whom did you entrust the investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interviews were carried out by Sadri Selca, while Hasan Gashi did this from the military police. And the fact that I've written here "Mejdin Gashi does not recognise his father," if we suppose that he is a security worker or a spy, his opinion here about his father shows that the person, the member of the brigade that is, distances himself from his own father. And I must have received this information again from my structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Can we move to another individual, please, Sanije Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if the witness could be given the blue file again and perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please assist him with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And would you be kind enough to turn him to tab 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you were exhibited this document as annex 19 to your 92 ter statement and it's been given proposed Exhibit Number P897. This is a report you tell us compiled by Sadri Selca on the 26th of August following an investigation into the disappearance and the death of Sanije Balaj. And the report says: "Sanije Balaj from Strellc i Poshtem was taken by Mete Krasniqi from the village of Vranoc. I do not remember the date. She was taken to the commander for an interview, and the commander then authorised Cufa to talk to her." Now, that reference to the commander, Witness 17, that is a reference to you, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Just to be clear, you've put this forward as your own security officer's investigation and it indicates that Sanije Balaj was taken by Mete Krasniqi to you for an interview. Now, let's be clear about this. When you saw that note, did you recognise it as accurate, that Mete Krasniqi had brought someone to you, a man with whom you say you do not cooperate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well is the note accurate then or is it wrong what Sadri Selca wrote down here? When you saw it, what do you think?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that he stopped Sanije Balaj. I spoke with Mete Krasniqi. He brought her to his office, and that's why I authorised Cufe Krasniqi to go there and talk to find the reasons why this girl was stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you knew that Mete Krasniqi had brought Sanije Balaj to Baran; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mete Krasniqi told me this himself and I mentioned earlier --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes let's --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- When this happened, when I met him in Qallapek.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let's not get confused. I'm not talking about after the event. I'm talking on the day that she was taken in by Mete Krasniqi, Witness 17. Now, this record indicates that she was taken by Mete Krasniqi to you. Was she taken to you by Mete Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So when you saw this in Sadri Selca's note, why didn't you say to him: This is plainly wrong, this isn't what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see the date, 26th of eighth, 1998. These notes were taken during the time when we began to withdraw from Lugu i Baranit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. But when you were looking at them and producing them in your 92 ter statement, why did you not say: It says there that Mete Krasniqi brought Sanije Balaj to me but that is plainly wrong because I never had any dealings with Mete Krasniqi at all? We had no contact whatsoever. Why didn't you say that in your 92 ter statement, Witness 17?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that misstates his own -- this witness's testimony in the 92 ter statement. In the 92 ter statement he admits to having contact with Mete on various occasions or at least one occasion concerning this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, the witness also made a distinction in time what happened at earlier stages and later so perhaps you could include --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I thought I corrected the witness's misapprehension in the last question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you saw this indicating that on the day in question Mete was brought to you, and you were referring to it in your statement why did you not say, that is wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Is he -- is Mr. Emmerson is now saying that Mete was brought to him because in the note --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's reformulate --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's a slip of the tongue and I apologise for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The note makes it clear that your security officer was indicating that Mete Krasniqi brought Sanije Balaj to you. And you have told us that you had no official contacts with Mete Krasniqi. What I want to know is when you saw this note why did you not say in your 92 ter statement that is not correct and it could not be corrected because I did not have such dealings with Mete Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last portion, Mr. Emmerson, should have been --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If the point is not helpful, then I'll take it in a different --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the question as such -- you said Sanije Balaj was not brought to me, irrespective of what kind of contacts you had with Mete Krasniqi. The question is where the report states that she was brought to you why you had not pointed at the incorrectness of that portion of the report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't asked. Now that you asked me the concrete question, I'm here to give you a very accurate reply. Sanije was never brought to me and I had no contacts whatsoever with this girl as far as this case is concerned. Why I did not mention this in the past, I said that I wasn't asked. But it is possible that the official who compiled the document was told that Sanije was brought to the offices of the commander. But I'm telling you that Sanije Balaj was never brought to my office. So this might be the mistake or the information is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Let me put another version to you which is slightly different. Cufe Krasniqi has testified before the Tribunal that whilst he was in the Baran barracks with you, Avni and Iber Krasniqi came to the two of you and told you that a woman had been detained on suspicion of collaboration. He says that they two, that is Avni and Iber Krasniqi, spoke to both of you about this woman and that you then assigned Cufe Krasniqi to interview her. That's transcript 5771 to 7. Is that true, that account? Did Avni and Iber Krasniqi come to you whilst you were in company with Cufe Krasniqi and say, We have detained a woman on suspicion of collaboration?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't -- I'm not aware of this, that they came to me. However, I had this information that a woman was there and I authorised Cufe to go and talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you've told us, I think, haven't you, that you did not regard Avni and Iber Krasniqi as part of your military police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They never were part of my police, my military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in fact in paragraph 80 of your 92 ter statement you described them as men who were hindering your activities, taking cars, and detaining civilians; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Why did you authorise the detention of a woman who'd been brought in by those two men, Witness 17?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that misstates this witness's testimony. He authorised Cufe to go and talk to her once he was informed she had been detained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's try to not lose ourselves in too much details. If someone is detained and if you authorise someone to interview the detainee and if you are the commander, then that implies acceptance of the situation of detention at that time. So therefore, let's try to focus on what it's really about and not about relatively unimportant details. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put the question to you again. Why in those circumstances did you authorise her continued detention, this woman who'd been arrested by Mete Krasniqi, who'd been brought to the barracks, and where Avni and Iber Krasniqi had come and brought her and raised her case with Cufe Krasniqi? Why did you authorise her continued detention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never authorised her detention. I authorised Cufe to go and check why she was there, but I couldn't have any control over the parallel structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. That involved Cufe, one of your officers, being sent to interview somebody brought in by Mete Krasniqi, did it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you still say you can't think of any legitimate reason why with your authorisation officers under your command would cooperate with Mete Krasniqi? Because on your evidence it seems that you've directed that they should.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. There was cooperation before the arrival of the brigade in Baran, and their private cooperation happened because they were from the same village, they knew each other very well, and I couldn't stop them from having those contacts. However, sending Cufe to see why the girl was there was because I wanted to know why she had been detained and why she had been sent to Mete's office. I wanted to know why?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. If we look back at Sadri Selca's note it says: "After Cufa released her, she was then taken to an unknown" -- I'm sorry. "She was taken by a person known as Galan ... and by Avni Krasniqi. She was then taken to an unknown place, but her liquidation was carried out by Galan. In all probability, Togeri, the lieutenant, took her to Lake Radoniq." Do you see that passage there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to ask you, please, to turn to tab 25 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And for this purpose we should be in private session, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm entirely in Your Honour's hands. We started I think at about 9.15. I'm entirely happy to run through the break. I've got about 30 minutes of questions to ask the witness about reports to Mr. Haradinaj allegedly made by him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, the Chamber will allow you another 20 minutes and gives you as guidance that sometimes when you are doing your -- making your best efforts to make a point that sometimes the Chamber understands already what point you are making and even before you think that you made the point, that the Chamber has taken the point already. That means that sometimes you could move to the next topic a bit earlier than you usually do. That's also the reason why we give you the 20 minutes --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I accept the rebuke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll have a break until five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 17, open in front of you is your witness statement made in November 2004. For the record, it's tab 34 and paragraph 144. In that paragraph you describe Idriz Balaj as the commander of the Black Eagles and then there are two sentences which read as follows. "I don't know of any incidents that were responsible for. Idriz Balaj in general terms did as he pleased, but I cannot give you anything concrete." And you wrote those words and signed that statement. Was that the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In the light of that I want to ask you some questions then, please, about the meeting that you suggest took place on the 21st of August, which you refer to in your 92 ter statement at paragraph 109, where you say you reported crimes against civilians committed by Idriz Balaj, Maliq Ndrecaj, and Faton Mehmetaj. Presumably if it's correct that you knew of no concrete allegations of any crimes committed by Idriz Balaj, you could not have communicate any allegations of specific crimes committed by Idriz Balaj to Ramush Haradinaj, could you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not speak to Ramush directly. Later we spoke about the disciplining of Idriz Balaj and the taking of measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Just to be clear, when you spoke on the 21st of August, 1998, to Ramush Haradinaj you did not and could not have told him about specific crimes committed by Idriz Balaj, could you, because you didn't know of any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I pointed out to him that he should discipline him because there were words that he was not behaving properly, and I also said earlier that letters came to the Prapaqan command about his behaviour, the villagers were complaining.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You also told us that the letters that came to the Prapaqan command contained no allegations of crimes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They contained complaints but not direct allegations for crimes. Tahir Zemaj was more informed about this than I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you were there at the meeting, and just so that we're absolutely clear you imply a criticism of Ramush Haradinaj for failing to discipline Idriz Balaj after the meeting of the 21st of August or failing to remove him, but it follows from the evidence that you've given, does it not, that you gave him no allegations with any specific crimes alleged which were capable of being investigated or resulting in disciplinary measures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we did not speak about such things because at that time, this was some kind of a taboo theme. People did not dare to raise such issues, but as regards the disciplining I told him that he should have been disciplined about the incident between me and Toger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, could we move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The same is true of Maliq Ndrecaj is it not, that at that meeting you made no specific allegations of crimes committed by Maliq Ndrecaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maliq Ndrecaj behaved improperly, and he did not obey what he was told to do and Tahir was responsible for him because it was -- he was in his area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Please answer my next question yes or no, Witness 17. At the meeting on the 21st of August, neither you nor Tahir Zemaj conveyed any allegations of specific crimes committed or allegedly committed by Maliq Ndrecaj, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And as far as Faton Mehmetaj is concerned perhaps you wouldn't mind briefly turning to tab 29 in the bundle. This is a document that you have produced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Similar from the floppy disk.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, in fact, this is a document which is annexed, I believe, to the witness's 92 ter statement. I'm just -- I do apologise. I've put to one side my index.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you move on and then we'll hear about the origin of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me ask you, please, to look at tab 29. This is an unsigned document which you referred to in your 92 ter statement dealing with the appointment of commanders after Tahir Zemaj had taken over as the overall commander. We can see that it is dated the 22nd of August and it bears Tahir Zemaj's name in type script at the bottom. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you confirm, please, then that after this meeting that you say that you had with Ramush Haradinaj on the 21st of August, Tahir Zemaj appointed Faton Mehmetaj as assistant for morale?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the meeting of the 20th of August, 1998, and the change of command or the joining up of all forces, Tahir Zemaj and Ramush Haradinaj agreed on the formation of the command, and it was Ramush's proposal that Faton Mehmetaj be an assistant for morale.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not asking you whose proposal it was. I'm simply asking you to confirm that on the 22nd of August, the day after the meeting that you have described with Ramush Haradinaj, Tahir Zemaj issued an order appointing Faton Mehmetaj as part of the staff with responsibility for morale; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document and the names are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I just want to ask you about one thing, if I can, please. You are listed there in this document as head of operational staff. Is that a role that you were given at that meeting, Witness 17?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not head but chief of operative staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that may simply be a translation issue. Would you look behind tab 30, please, and can I ask you -- because the document we've just been looking at behind tab 29, produced by you is unsigned. The one behind tab 30 bears a signature. Is that the signature of Tahir Zemaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be, yes, it can be.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, in all respects this document is identical to the one that you have produced- and can I indicate there's an error in the translation. The English translation of the communique starts with the words: "On the 28th of August," it should read as you see on the original: "On the 20th of August." In all respects, this document is identical except it is signed and your name isn't on it as Chief of Staff. The name of Sali Veseli seems to have been appointed Chief of Staff by the document signed by Mr. Zemaj. Can you help us about that, please. How does your name come to be on the other list and his on this one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain in detail. Ramush knows that this is what they agreed on with Tahir, but Sali Veseli at the time was not present in Kosova. He was sent to Albania for organisational purposes at the order of Ramush Haradinaj, and Ramush himself said that if he does not return in time we will have this change. That's why the change was made of point 3, which means the chief of operative staff because Sali Veseli did not come on time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think -- I want, if I may, just go briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if the usher could just take the witness to tab 34 again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is the statement, Witness 17, that you made in November of 2004 and could he please be taken to paragraph 120. I want to ask you about the last sentence of paragraph 120 of your November 2004 witness statement where you say this: "Din Krasniqi is a paediatrician and was either the self-proclaimed commander of Baran or was appointed by KLA Commander Ramush Haradinaj." Now, you told us yesterday you had no personal knowledge of the system of appointment, but I wonder how you can help us, if you can, please, to reconcile that statement in your witness statement with the testimony you gave yesterday, that Din Krasniqi told you himself that he had been appointed by Ramush Haradinaj. Why, if that was told to you, in terms, did you say in your November 2004 statement that he was either the self-proclaimed commander or had been appointed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because with the arrival of the brigade at Baran he continued to perform his post and refused to enter the structure of the brigade and become one with us. That's why during the meetings with him he would state that Ramush appointed him, but I didn't have any official document that would prove his words right. This is why I'm saying here that he was either a self-proclaimed commander or appointed by Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith -- oh, Mr. Harvey. You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Harvey, who's counsel for Mr. Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness -- good morning, Witness 17. As His Honour has just explained, I represent Lahi Brahimaj. Can we just agree on one or two things at the outset. You never knew Lahi Brahimaj before September of 1998, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would say before September.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You first met him in a meeting that was attended by Hashim Thaqi; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To my recollection, it occurred in Prapaqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: We'll come to the date of that meeting in a little while. You personally never went to Jabllanice, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, I never went there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry for the interruption. Your Honours, we're back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a group of paramilitaries called Arkan's Tigers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not personally, but I've heard about them and their activities in Bosnia and Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And referring to their activities in Kosovo, they were known for being a group of individuals who massacred, murdered, and engaged in committing serious crimes against the population of the Kosovar people, correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object as to relevance unless my colleague can tie it specifically somehow to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I can and I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then with this clear commitment, Mr. Kearney, I suggest that we'll wait and see what the next questions will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you have my question in mind, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The massacres committed by the paramilitary and mercenary forces of Serbia and the forces of Arkan I'm well aware of those massacres, and it is more than true what you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're talking about the reputation at this moment, not about any personal knowledge. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In your statement in 2004 you indicated that you had heard that Idriz Balaj - and this is paragraph 145 - participated with Arkan's Tigers in Bosnia. First of all, who did you get this information from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned - and I will repeat it again - this is what I heard. There were rumours about this. I'm not saying that it is accurate. It was said, there were rumours, that he did take part. I did hear these rumours, but I don't remember from whom. I believe it was upon our entering Kosova in 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, if the witness confirms now that it's rumours, where he even says: "I don't know where I heard about the rumours," and then that he immediately adds that whether it's true or not, then if it stays at this level --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Then I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we don't have to focus --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't pursue it any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think the point is made generally in terms of rumours and my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you know of an individual by the name of Gani Gjukaj? I believe he, if I'm not mistaken, was a FARK soldier, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a FARK officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I see, a FARK officer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss the Sanije Balaj incident and situation with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm going to read something from a statement that he made to the Office of the Prosecutor, this is behind tab 27, specifically paragraph 22, and ask whether or not you ever heard the same information that he speaks to, which is here --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, counsel, did you say tab 27? It's not behind mine, my tab 27 is a decision --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In the blue binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I find 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: My mistake. I'm a little colour-blind right now, Your Honour, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's purplish-blue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It cannot be treated as colour-blindness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: "I never heard the name "Toger" associated with the disappearance of Sanije Balaj. I would meet with Toger and he respected and listened to me. Toger was a great warrior and was very disciplined. He was perhaps more aggressive than some others."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please finish reading the rest of the paragraph, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Surely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: "Only one or two people wore black uniforms." My first question is: Did you ever receive any information - and now I'm asking you for a negative here - that no one had ever mentioned Toger being associated with the disappearance of Sanije Balaj?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is a question, Mr. Guy-Smith, which could create a lot of confusion. Whether positively someone heard that it was never -- so someone saying --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see the slippery path as you begin --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- And I'll leave it alone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And finally, in your 92 ter statement at paragraph 110 you indicated that you went to Toger's headquarters in Irzniq and that the headquarters was in a former school on the edge of the village on an elevated site, and it is that particular statement that I wish to question you about, that the headquarters was in a former school on the edge of the village on an elevated site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: May we scroll down just a little further, Your Honour, so the witness can read the sentence that's being presented to him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I suggest to you that that was not the headquarters of Toger, it was never the headquarters of Toger, whether or not you had a meeting there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had meetings in Irzniq, and that's a fact. Our meetings were held in the Irzniq school, and present for Ramush, Toger, and other people who were involved in these issues. The school in Irzniq, everybody knows where it is and that's where we had our meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I appreciate that. My point to you, sir, is that the headquarters of Toger were not at that school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that it wasn't, but I believe that after the fall of Gllogjan on the 11th of August, during that offensive, they retreated and then Toger came and established his headquarters in the school in Irzniq. I think this is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And finally, sir, apart from the fact that you had heard rumours about Toger being associated with Arkan's Tigers in Bosnia, did you ever receive any information whatsoever that Idriz Balaj had ever been in Bosnia at all in any function, let alone a military one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. I don't know anything about this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. I'm looking at the clock. We'll have a break now until five minutes past 1.00. Mr. Kearney would then have 40 minutes remaining. How much time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Hopefully not all of that, Your Honour. Hopefully I can get it done in 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you could try and squeeze it in as good as you can. Then there's another matter. The Chamber would like to be informed whether there are any objections to the annexes to the 92 ter statement so we don't have a debate once the witness has left us. I remember that number 18, Mr. Guy-Smith, you might not insist on it being excluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have been actually persuaded by the combined efforts of the Prosecution and the Defence that I would not -- that I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- Retract my previous position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's any other annex which would find objections from the Defence, then the Chamber would like to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There's certainly an objection in relation to I think it's annex 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 17, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The bulk of that, Mr. Kearney, as I understood, had agreed to remove unless I've got my numbers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then my next request would be that the Chamber be informed about any agreement on the part of annex 17 being removed and whether there's agreement on that. I further inform the parties that the attempts to see whether we could deal with the next witness tomorrow, that although there is a courtroom available that it might not easy to compose a CLSS team for such a hearing but I have not given up hope yet. We -- Mr. Harvey. I'm informed that you would not be available. You would try to find out whether Mr. Troop is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I am trying to find out that he is, Your Honour. I do know that we have an important meeting that is scheduled with our client. You realise it is difficult to do this during the ordinary working week the course of week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And we have a very important witness coming up from our standpoint next week that we wish to meet with our client about tomorrow and that had been booked from 12.00 until 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: We will obviously try and work with the Court in every way that we can but I do urge on, Your Honour, that this is a matter of considerable importance to the defence of Mr. Brahimaj that that meeting should be able to take place tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which leaves it open, you said from 1.00 to 3.00?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So a late start might help you out?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It might.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just -- we do not know. We also have a reschedule meetings, et cetera. We have a break until ten minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any agreement to be reported on annex 17?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have spoke to my colleague. I think in an abundance of caution we're going to need the evening to read through to see if we can compare items down from that. If we can notify the Court and our colleagues either later tonight or tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But none of the others are objected to? Mr. Harvey, I'm looking to you as well. I know that the line that those who do not respond agree is a disputed line, especially if they appear in statements --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No silence, no silence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No silence. Mr. Kearney, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 17, good afternoon. Witness 17, I want to ask you some more questions about Sadri Selca's notes. You were asked in yesterday's session at great length by Mr. Emmerson about certain events that were chronicled in those notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And I'd like to, Your Honours, if I may, call up annex 18 to the 92 ter statement at this stage and I'd like to present --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give the provisional exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And I'll be referring to page 13 or -- excuse me, page 8 of the English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: You're speaking of P896?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes and I would ask -- that's the right page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 17, yesterday it was suggested to you by Mr. Emmerson that the final entry on this page, referring to Istref Krasniqi from Turjake, was an entry reflecting a detention conducted by Mr. Selca. I want to follow-up on that, if I may. Do you know for certain if that entry relating to Mr. Krasniqi refers to an actual detention by Sadri Selca or is it simply his reporting the results of one of his investigations --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I object to the form of the question. It's being put in the form of a suggestion. The witness was asked to comment on this passage and he said in his testimony that it was clear that this was an individual who had been detained, as the others had been detained. And for Mr. Kearney now to put suggestions to the witness in a leading form in re-examination in our submission is unhelpful and not a proper way to re-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the reason why I'm pursuing this line of questioning is I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not the line of questioning, it's the form of the questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I believe, given the conduct of my colleague related to this entry, it is important to give this witness a chance to clarify that answer. And if I can be allowed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay what you can do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- If you then draw the attention of the witness to what he said yesterday and then you invite him to make any further comments as to what his testimony yesterday. That would be the appropriate way of doing it. And if you could guide me to the relevant page of yesterday, Mr. Kearney, that would certainly assist me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's page -- transcript page 7678.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 17, I'd like to ask you - this is at line 5 on page 7678 - I'd like to read you a question and answer from yesterday's testimony about this passage. "Q. This is a list of people that Sadri Selca is recorded as having been brought into your barracks for questioning, isn't it?" Your answer is: "Yes, of course, he must have brought in these people because he has kept these notes after the talks or conversations with them as it appears from what I see." Now, my question relates to the language you use in your answer, namely, "he must have brought in these people ..." I want to ask you relating to this last entry in annex 18 if you know that Istref Krasniqi was brought in by Sadri Selca for questioning to your barracks in Baran?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not that sure where he had his conversation. I said that he must have brought him there because he had an office in the Baran barracks. Whether he had been detained or not, that does not stand. I reject that. These notes are Sadri Selca's note -- notes, not mine. It was alleged here that they are mine but they are not. He gave them to me and I submitted them to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer, Witness 17. I'd like to follow-up. You said that: "Whether he had been detained or not, that does not stand, I reject that." Could you please explain that answer for the Trial Chambers. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first ask the witness what he personally knows about the whole matter apart from having read the notes because that seems to be the issue. You have given this document to the Office of the Prosecution, you have been read what it says about Imer Krasniqi from the village of Turjake, Peje, was taken regarding his collaboration with the Serbian police and several other cases. What do you personally know about Imer Krasniqi taken for an interview, apart from what you read here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing else, and there's nothing in my mind about his being brought there. I cannot say anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: In items -- the item referring to Imer Krasniqi as item 19 on that page, in both items 17 and 18 Sadri Selca specifically notes, quoting: "The two individuals that are the subject of those paragraphs were brought to Baran by the military police of the 3rd/131st Brigade." Now, the 3rd/131st Brigade is your brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 131st Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And there were occasions that you know of personally when Sadri Selca brought individuals into your brigade for questioning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was his task. He had that responsibility and he carried out that task. That happened in some cases, but interviews cannot be called detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: My question to you, Witness 17, is simply this: In paragraph 19 there's no reference to this gentleman, Mr. Krasniqi, being brought into the military police headquarters of the 3rd/131st Brigade. Is that correct? Am I reading that document correctly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, if the witness would say "no," then it make -- the Chamber would not accept such an answer. If the Chamber says -- if the witness says "yes," then he confirms something the Chamber can read as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I add that this is an extract from a long list that begins two pages earlier, in some of which is there is a specific reference to individuals people and in others there is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but this is comment on how Mr. Kearney -- what his references for his questioning. And we'll leave that to Mr. Kearney. At the same time, we can read that there's no reference to the brigade here. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You had also specifically tasked Sadri Selca to investigate illegal abductions and executions being conducted by the KLA; is that a -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assigned him as the person responsible for security, and he had to check all the irregularities that were going on and keep evidence on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, this note that was entered into Mr. Selca's notes occurred on 4 September 1998; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At this point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- I'm going to object to leading. This is a document that was proffered by the Prosecution with their witness, and at this point it's inappropriate for him to be leading on re-direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time asking a lot of questions about what we all read in this report -- I mean, of course it could be that something has been left out after the entry of the 4th of September, but we find under 11, 2nd of September, we find below 14, before 15, we find the 4th of September. So unless there's any specific reason to believe that this is incorrect, there's no need to further ask about it, just as there should be no real objection against leading in this respect. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you for that guidance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 17, this Trial Chamber has heard evidence that Istref and Nurije Krasniqi were abducted at midnight on 12 July 1998 by four soldiers of the UCK and never seen again alive. I want to ask you if on 12 July 1998 Sadri Selca was working in your brigade as a military police investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether he was there on the 12th of July. I think he came later there because the 12th of July is the date when the brigade went there, to Baran.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Isn't the 12th of July, Witness 17, your first actual day in the Baran Valley?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: On your first day in the Baran Valley, did you dispatch four men to Turjake to abduct and execute the Krasniqis?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm not at all clear what the thrust of this question is. The entry at 19 has nothing to do with Nurije and Istref Krasniqi being taken from anywhere; it has to do with their son, Imer Krasniqi, being taken in for questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: It has to do with Istref being abducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With the greatest of respect, it's plain from the text itself. "Imer (Istref)" means Imer, son of Istref Krasniqi, was taken in for interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we would not comment on what it means, whereas many useless questions are put to the witness here, there is a matter where we could try to find out how the witness aware of what was usually done, how he understands this. And of course he has given already evidence on how the names were listed of the soldiers. We could ask him whether he understood this, in view of all the other entries, to reflect the same system.
