Why -- Witness 17, the entry under 9 - is it on the screen for the witness? Yes - the entrance under 9 says "Imer (Istref) Krasniqi," how do you understand this? To what person does this refer, since we have one first name within brackets and another one just there. How do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand it this way: Imer is the name, Istref is the name of his father, and Krasniqi is the name of the surname.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now when reading this line, do you understand that the son only was taken for an interview or that the son together with the father or the father alone was taken for an interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only the son, Imer; Istref is the father. So Imer (Istref) Krasniqi, and this is just one person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: In any event, Witness 17, Sadri Selca was not working as your brigade security officer on 12 July 1998; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, before that date of 12 July, had you ever even been to the Baran Valley before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Without telling us where, without telling us your village or your municipality, you grew up in a completely separate part of Kosovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Before that day, 12 July, have you ever been to Vranoc, Luka, or Prapaqan before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Before your arrival to the Baran Valley in early July of 1998, had you ever met Mete Krasniqi before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Din Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Avni Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Him neither.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you know at that time that Avni, when you first arrived in the Baran Valley, that Avni was the brother of Mete Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And you've already told us that all three of the accused were people that, before late June of 1998 when you arrived in Kosovo, you didn't know them either. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, yesterday - this is at transcript page 7708, Your Honour, lines 9 through 12 - Mr. Emmerson tried to suggest to you that your testimony about parallel structures was an attempt by you to deflect criticism for failing to control officers under your command. I want to ask you: Was there a parallel structure in the Baran Valley separate from your brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the military police is concerned, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I'd like to draw or pull up annex 13, this is proposed Prosecution Exhibit 892. I'd like to show the witness, if we may, the first page of this exhibit which is ERN U0015988. And of course it is page 1 in the English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 17, you were asked at length yesterday about whether Din Krasniqi had direct contact with Ramush Haradinaj after your arrival to the Baran Valley. Now, I'd like you to look at this document. This is a document on -- dated Vranoc, 29 July 1998, a working meeting of the Baran Valley staff. The first paraphrase reference to an individual talking in that meeting is to an individual named Doktori. I want to ask you if, based on your own knowledge of pseudonyms and personalities in the Baran Valley in July of 1998, you know who Doktori is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Doktori was Din Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, this is almost -- this meeting was almost three weeks after you assumed command of the Baran Valley. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If you consider the 12th, it is roughly three weeks after.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Were you invited to this meeting, Witness 17?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. I did not attend this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, the title of this document refers to the Baran Valley staff. At this time, 29 July 1998, did you even know that there was a Baran Valley staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that when we arrived on the 12th of July there was an existing staff. Din was the leader in Baran, and with our arrival it meant that all the villages should become part of the brigade, should become one. But Din continued to practice like in the past. He called on the local commanders at least once a week to have meetings with them. So I could say that there was always a sort of parallelism going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'd like you to, if we may, look at and scroll down at the same time, look at pages 2, 3, and 4. There are references to several village representatives talking at this meeting, and I'm just going to read through them Raushiq, Vranoc, Turjake, Qallapek, going now to page 3 Kosuriq, Ljuga, page 4, Nepolje, Loxha, Gradac, Zllopak, Doberdol. Were those villages that within your own AOR, Witness 17?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And with permission, I'd like to go back if I may, Your Honour, to page 1 of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention, Witness 17, to the first few paragraphs of page 1 where there are -- there's a statement by the -- by Din Krasniqi being made and then by the Baran Valley chief. I'm going to refer you specifically to the comments about combat morale that Doktori makes in the first sentence, expected areas of enemy attack he makes in the second sentence. And then under the heading "Baran Valley chief," the discussion of weapons in the first sentence and the discussion of readiness in the second sentence. I would like to ask you, are those issues that were relevant to you as the brigade commander in that AOR?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were in the interests of the brigade and the village commands informed us every evening in the brigade about what was going on, while Din summoned them once a week. But this was done without my knowledge, without my authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, beyond the -- this direct contact that Din Krasniqi was having with Mr. Haradinaj, did Din Krasniqi, to your knowledge, also have direct contact with either Idriz Balaj or Faton Mehmetaj?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to be absolutely clear. If Mr. Kearney is seeking to rely on this document as being the basis for the suggestion that there was ongoing direct contact, then plainly it is a document that shows attendance attendant a single meeting and the witness has already testified to the source of his knowledge so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm aware, but there is nothing in the question that suggests that it was an ongoing contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see. Now, beyond this direct contact was having --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "Was having," that's my concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was having -- had, if you make that had, and explore if there was anything more than this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And I believe the witness gave evidence about the other sources of his information about these contacts yesterday. I want to pursue it further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although it does not -- to say that the evidence there would be very much supportive of ongoing contacts would be an overstatement. He gave evidence on that. It's clearly in my mind. And now you're putting to him the record of what seems to be one meeting where both were present. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 17, beyond this direct contact that Din Krasniqi had with Mr. Haradinaj, did Din Krasniqi to your knowledge also have direct contact after your arrival in the Baran Valley with Idriz Balaj and Faton Mehmetaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: In paragraph 59 of your witness statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Can we bring that up, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could that be brought on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I question only at this point whether or not Mr. Kearney seeks to impeach his own witness or is going to attempt to obtain a clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll see what his question is and then we'll most likely find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 17, I'd like to direct your attention to, I believe, the fourth full sentence in paragraph 59 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it -- wasn't that a line on which you agreed that it should be --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, exactly so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because I've got it on my notes here that the line starting with: "I believe" and ending with "Faton Mehmetaj" was a line to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: To be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- To be redacted. So therefore that's out so therefore it's no use to take the witness to that statement because it's not in his statement anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: My understanding of the Court's ruling that I was allowed to seek any foundation for this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I -- if you -- you've asked the witness whether -- you asked the witness as a matter of fact just a second ago whether he had any direct contact; the answer was no. So as a matter of fact -- I don't know what you would like to further explore --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I can rephrase the question, Your Honour, in a different manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so. And let's take the 92 ter statement from the screen at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 17, you told us yesterday that you received information from a village commander that Din Krasniqi and Ramush Haradinaj had contact with each other after your arrival in the Baran Valley. I want to ask you if you received any similar information regarding Din Krasniqi having contact with either Idriz Balaj or Faton Mehmetaj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The contact between Din Krasniqi and Ramush and the information by the village commanders may bear fruit because he was in that meeting that we mentioned. And during the meetings that we held in the evening, he reported about these contacts. As for Idriz Balaj and Faton Mehmetaj, I don't remember the source of the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of what information exactly, Witness 17?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean the contact itself, whether they did have contacts or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You -- earlier a question was put to you: "Did Din Krasniqi to your knowledge also have direct contact after your arrival in the Baran Valley with Idriz Balaj and Faton Mehmetaj?" Your answer was: "I have no knowledge about this." Now it seems that you are now telling something quite different from that. Did you have knowledge or did you have no knowledge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I'm saying is that as to where this information that there were contacts between them came from, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It never reached you; do I understand you correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will say it again I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, please proceed. I'm looking at the clock. I know that we are already a couple minutes over time. Mr. Kearney, is it possible to finish in, let's say, the next ten minutes. Then I could ask the cooperation of the interpreters, transcriber, technicians -- let me just ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What need would there be to put further questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As matters stand, none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At the present time, there would be no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So far so good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, could you finish in the next ten minutes and then a message will be sent to the Chamber who will sit in Courtroom I that we had a late finish. Is that a possibility?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 17, I want to talk to you about Mete Krasniqi for a moment. I'd like to be clear. Do you know where Mete Krasniqi's office was in Baran in July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not within the scope of the school-yard or the brigade; barracks outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you even know, sir, if he had an office?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's cut matters short here. The question was not where he did not have an office; the question was where he had an office. Could you tell us? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When Cufe Krasniqi was sent there, I noticed that the office was in Baran, but outside the scope of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At what distance, approximately, from where the brigade was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was very near.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How near? I mean "very near" could be 20 metres, a hundred metres, 300 metres. Could you give us a better indication.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between 20 to 50 metres one would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: It was suggested both yesterday and today, Witness 17, that on some level you and Mete Krasniqi cooperated with each other or worked together in investigations. Did he try at some point to join your military police unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He wanted to become a member, but I did not put him on the list of military police members; because of this, I was threatened. He came to my office and threatened me in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you refused to put him on the list for your own military police office or officers' unit, how did he threaten you? What did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came in the facilities of the brigade, he wanted to come to the office. I told the guard to give him permission to come to my office. It was only the two of us in my office, and he said to me the following, Because of not making me a member of the military police, in case I commit an act of betrayal --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreter did not hear the last part of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last part of your sentence on from where you said: "In case I commit an act of betrayal ..." And then what followed. The interpreters couldn't catch your words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He said, If I commit an act of betrayal I will commit that against you and I will liquidate you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- Quickly interject. I don't know whether the Chamber is aware of the fact -- and I'm objecting on the grounds of hearsay because this gentleman is dead, the author of the statement is dead and I don't know whether or not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. It causes a certain number of problems in terms of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, problems to verify statements given by persons who do not live anymore are well-known to the Chamber. Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You were asked at great length about the Sanije Balaj. Did you hold Mete Krasniqi responsible in your mind for that disappearance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said earlier that I met him at the police station in Qallapek. I took him by his arm. I asked him whispering in the ear, Where is Sanije. And he said I handed her over to two persons. And I replied, The first person to be held responsible for this will be you because you were the one who first stopped her. And this was the reason why he threatened me together with him not becoming part of the military police list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you initiate an investigation into the Sanije Balaj disappearance, Witness 17?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From what I had heard and from my question that I put to Mete, I ordered Sadri to start an investigation into the matter, but with the formation of the Joint Command in Prapaqan, within the framework of the Joint Command, a certain process, investigative process, into the case of Sanije Balaj began and it was carried out by two persons, one called Gashi and the second Tigri. These two persons initiated the investigation in the case of Sanije Balaj. Now I've remembered Gashi's first name Hysen Gashi and Commander Tigri.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I want to direct your attention to the 20th of August meeting in Prapaqan with the 68 village commanders. You were questioned about the statements of the author, the journalist, who we talked about earlier and his statement in that meeting about the fish in Lake Radonjic getting fat on human flesh. And you brought up the fact that -- or it was brought up to you that Din Krasniqi raised perhaps some complaints during that meeting. I want to ask you specifically: When the comment about the fish getting fat at Lake Radoniq was made, did Din Krasniqi say anything in response to that comment that you heard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Briefly before the witness answers, that question was put to the witness twice in terms --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Also by the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On both occasions he said he could not remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question has been put by the Bench to the witness, Mr. Kearney, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, I do. And I would like to ask another related question in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 17, when that statement was made about the fish, what was the reaction that you saw in the room from the 68 village commanders who were present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that there were a reaction, neither from Din or -- nor from anybody else. But when you speak of such things, these are very grave matters. It was a shuddering thing to say, but I didn't see any comments or any reactions. I mentioned it earlier, that this was a questionable issue and to discuss it in an open forum was very difficult and it was not very logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You were asked also on cross-examination about the 21 August meeting that you had with Tahir Zemaj and Ramush Haradinaj in Prapaqan, and you were asked if you had given any specifics to Mr. Haradinaj about misconduct of any of his soldiers. And I believe you said you gave no specifics. I want to ask you simply: During that meeting did you inform Mr. Haradinaj --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I object to the form of the question before it even finishes. It's plainly a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is foundational, it's my last question, I'm doing that to save time, the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please put the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you inform Mr. Haradinaj during that meeting of the assassination plot that was outstanding against Tahir Zemaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was done by Tahir directly because we had information and notes that a plot was being prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And the information you had in that regard referred to Faton Mehmetaj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And can you tell us what Faton Mehmetaj's relationship was with Mr. Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning it was said that he was in charge of the military police in the Gllogjan staff, and then after the Joint Command was established in the Dukagjini Plain he was political representative of the Dukagjini Plain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, you told us that you would finish in ten minutes. Far more minutes have elapsed since then. Therefore, if there would be one single question, I'll allow you to put it to the witness, but otherwise we'll finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During that meeting when you brought this assassination plot up to Mr. Haradinaj's attention and you brought the general allegations about Toger as well, what did he tell you in response to those two items?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand "you" to be in the plural here rather than single.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm concerned of what about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have -- we have to come to a conclusion --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: This is my last question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How did Mr. Haradinaj respond to what Tahir Zemaj told him about the assassination plot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even when I related to him about Idriz Balaj's incident in Luka, even in this case as well he said, I will look into the situation and these things won't happen. This was some kind of a promise that he made that these things would not happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kearney, then unfortunately I have to tell you that this concludes the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any further need on the basis of --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I would like to ask just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Really one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Really one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was that promise then the reason why the following day Tahir Zemaj agreed to incorporate Faton Mehmetaj's part of his command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Ramush's proposal and there was an agreement between the two; I mentioned it earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know whether this assassination plot had got something to do with Tahir Zemaj agreeing to that proposal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I couldn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. I'm looking to you, Mr. Guy-Smith, I'm looking to you, Mr. Harvey. I don't see any response, which I take it for that you have no further questions for the witness. Then, Witness 17, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming. Please -- perhaps you stay where you are at this moment due to the face distortion so that we don't have to pull the curtains down at this very moment. We have no time to deal with the exhibits at this moment. The Chamber would like to hear about exhibits -- attachment 17 to the 92 ter statement. We'll deal with the exhibits later. We do understand that there are no objections against the other attachments. Then there is an issue about the next witness from what I understand. Since we could not start or even finish the examination of the present witness today, tomorrow we would have only one hour and a half. We have to deal with protective measures, some examination-in-chief, the Chamber also in view of what rescheduling is required to have that witness tomorrow has decided although we usually try to get witnesses sent home before the weekend that it would be a fruitless effort in this case. And since VWS has informed us that the witness could stay over the weekend - which doesn't say that that's the witness who will testify immediately after the weekend, because I do understand that the witness coming next might be limited in -- as far as his availability is concerned. We'll deal with all that perhaps tomorrow, further exchange of views on how to proceed at the beginning of next week, also to resolve whatever disclosure issues are still outstanding. And we adjourn until the 3rd of April -- 3rd of September, quarter past 2.00, in this same courtroom. And I'd like to thank you for having come to The Hague to have answered all the questions of the parties and of the Bench. I wish everyone a good weekend.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 3rd day of September, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.07 p.m.,
